insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution; this protocol settles at ~$0.10 per verified receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that exists because the receipt eliminates the attribution problem rather than solving it.

Cookies, device fingerprinting, and third-party data brokers are all degrading simultaneously, and first-party data is blind to everything outside a single ecosystem — verified receipt signals operate outside all three failure modes.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither sees the full wallet. At 5,071 cryptographically verified receipts across categories, this dataset captures the cross-ecosystem signal that no single retailer can build internally.

insights.topic: Physical commerce dominance in the signal set
insights.insight: 78%+ of receipts in the current 14-day window are brick-and-mortar — restaurants, grocery, department stores, gas — which is precisely the offline purchase behavior that digital ad tech has historically been unable to verify.

insights.topic: Data quality ceiling at 11% unresolved merchants
insights.insight: One in nine receipts currently fails merchant classification, landing in an 'Unknown' bucket with a $290 average transaction value that likely reflects high-ticket or B2B spend — until merchant resolution improves, cross-domain and category-level signals carry a known accuracy ceiling.

Token velocity dropped week-over-week (0.694x) while acceleration held above 1x — fewer receipts per cycle but the trend line holds slope, which is a more durable foundation for data reliability than a spike-driven growth pattern.
